newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police remove immigrants from church.
newsitem.headline: French police remove immigrants from church.

text.p: Police evicted on Sunday about 400 Asian immigrants, most of them Chinese, from a Paris church they occupied on Saturday to demand residence rights.
Police broke through a side door at dawn to enter the Saint-Jean Baptiste Catholic church and negotiate with protesters who said they agreed to leave on condition that no arrest would be made.
Paris mayor Jean Tiberi ordered the church evacuated, saying the occupation by the immigrants and their children raised safety and sanitary problems.
The protest began on Sunday, coinciding with a large demonstration by intellectuals, civil rights activists, artists and left-wingers against a bill to toughen immigration regulations.
The protest, in the heavily Asian immigrant district of Belleville, mirrored last year's occupation of another church by dozens of African "sans papiers" (without documents) immigrants.
That protest lasted for more than two months and acutely embarrassed the government who sent police to break down the church gates and eject the Africans.
"Sans papiers" immigrants claim a stiffening of immigration regulations has deprived them of residence rights and demand to be given residence permits.
